description: This World Bank report evaluates the Nepal Irrigation and Water Resources Management Project, financed by International Development Association grants and credits of US$50 million plus additional financing of US$14.3 million, US$20 million and US$30 million. The project aimed to raise irrigated agriculture productivity and improve management of selected schemes, about 214 farmer-managed irrigation systems covering some 26,808 hectares mainly in the hill regions, and to strengthen institutions for integrated water resources management. It was implemented by Nepal's agriculture and water resources departments and the Water and Energy Commission Secretariat, approved on 30 September 2008 and closed on 30 June 2018 after its closing date was extended from 2013. The implementation completion and results report, number ICR00004144 of 12 December 2018, was prepared by the World Bank's Agriculture Global Practice for the South Asia region and gives ratings, results, costs and lessons. Coverage is Nepal. The 61-page PDF is free on the World Bank documents site. Caveats: it is the Bank's own evaluation, the cover still carries the original restricted distribution notice, and benefits rest on project monitoring data. For simulation it gives costs, areas and results of rehabilitating farmer-managed irrigation, useful for investment appraisal of rural water infrastructure. It is related to the FAO AQUASTAT irrigation investment costs record in this catalogue.
